newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan New Asia gets $17mln China power plant loan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan New Asia gets $17mln China power plant loan.

text.p: Taiwan's New Asia Construction and Development on Thursday signed a seven-year US$17 million syndicated loan package to finance a power plant it is building in China, company executives said.
The loans were organised by ABN AMRO Bank and Taiwan's International Commercial Bank of China, a New Asia official said by telephone.

The official confirmed that the loan package was signed but declined to disclose details or confirm local media reports that the power station to be built at Nantong in central Jiangsu province would start up in 1998.

Other Taiwan business groups, including the island's biggest conglomerate, Formosa Plastics, have shown interest in China's voracious energy market but have frozen plans to build major power plants under pressure from Taiwan's government.
Taipei urges investors to approach the communist mainland slowly, warning that Nationalist-ruled Taiwan otherwise risks becoming dangerously overdependent on its longtime arch rival.
Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs approved New Asia's application in May, the first approval for a major Taiwan-funded power station on the mainland.
Taiwan allows local firms in principle to build power plants in China, but has limited approvals to investors who are not involved in Taiwan's domestic power industry.
All local businesses must apply for Taiwan government approval before investing in China, Taiwan's rival since a civil war separated them in 1949.
